steps.text: 4:11 P.M. \ Overcast, Visibility: 10 km
Rhodes Island Landship, Medical Cabin

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Remove the electrodes.

options: What's the prognosis?
My head feels hot and distended. Not good.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No new developments.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You'll feel better after a quick rest.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, I've scanned your brain seven times over the past month or so, and the results are always the same.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There's nothing wrong with your medial temporal lobe, and the neurons in other brain areas are as active as they are in most young people.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Meaning you don't need to come to Medical for these unpleasant tests so often.

options: Then, what's wrong with my memory?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There's no doubt that you've lost a lot of your memory. Even someone like you wouldn't be able to manipulate the results.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Those memories are episodic, chiefly concerning the subjective awareness of your identity, and even more so about all your experiences before you fell asleep in the Chernobog sarcophagus.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In contrast, your procedural memory has recovered extremely quickly.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: From my reports or Amiya's and Dobermann's observations, this conclusion is clear.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your ability to command, as exhibited during the Chernobog incident, is not significantly worse than before.

options: Why would this happen?
In other words, I'm still useful?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There are many reasons for memory loss. Some are force majeure, others are subjective.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Medical testing can only rule out qualitative pathological changes.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Of course, you don't make as much noise as you used to.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Considering your language center has not been damaged, I can only guess that the deprivation of episodic memory has caused some changes in your personality.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: To Rhodes Island, you are far more than just 'useful.'

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Even if you truly lost all your memories and become an ignorant bystander, Amiya would not have regretted saving you, and there will always be a place for you at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In any case, I believe that the skills you possess will play just as key a role as they did in the past.

options: I want to be able to help you.
I want to be able to help Amiya.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And I've seen how hard you've been working.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: After leaving Lungmen, we've been making our way through the wastelands for some time. The operators need an opportunity to rest, Amiya in particular.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Likewise, you also need a chance to catch your breath, don't you?

options: I just want some time to adjust.
I don't want to stop here.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: With PRTS to help you, it won't take long for you to adapt to your work at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: However, I don't want you to push yourself.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Rhodes Island is not the only thing that has just emerged from a terrible disaster. You have as well, Dr. {@nickname}.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your physical indicators have more or less returned to normal, but your memory is still damaged, and your mental state is unstable.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As a patient, overwork can only harm you.

options: You're also a patient.
Amiya is also a patient.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Me? I appreciate your concern.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Though I can't say I'm used to Oripathy, I can assure you that I'm the last person you should worry about.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Amiya knows you're concerned about her, and she's been paying more attention to her health lately.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I have no choice but to admit, there are some areas in which your words hold more weight than mine.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, in the span of one short month, you've taken over the staffing of several departments on this ship.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In addition, I've seen you reviewing past battles together with combat operators to further explore the possibilities of tactical optimization.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You've even been reading during this entire examination. Are you looking at the briefing submitted by the new operator who just reported in a few days ago?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Furthermore, I've seen your notes.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Those records about even the most trivial of the operators' details, those flashes of tactical inspiration...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Those calculations for determining Rhodes Island's business efficiency, and even those scrawls that I can't make sense of. They are all evidence of your commitment to your duty.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Although most of these tasks can be completed with the assistance of PRTS, I think this is your preferred method.

options: It's just a way of organizing my thoughts.
PRTS's data lacks a bit of that human touch.
You didn't see me badmouthing you, did you?!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As the density of your notes increases, your cognition also improves.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: PRTS is just a tool. Avoiding overreliance on tools is a good working habit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So that was a complaint? I would rather take those words as a compliment.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: All of your abilities are recovering rapidly, not only due to the retention of your procedural memory, but also due to your extraordinary efforts.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Conscious exercise will help your brain return more quickly to your pre-comatose state, and may even bring back your memory faster than expected.

options: Do you want me to recover as quickly as possible?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I am your doctor. There's not a doctor out there who does not wish for the quick recovery of her patient.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That said, if you end up collapsing due to overwork, you'll disrupt Amiya's condition as well.

options: Are you only concerned about Amiya?
I see. You do care about me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: These sentiments of yours that occasionally leak through are quite unlike the past you. While this is rather intriguing, if I am the object of your feelings, let's just say we've no need of that.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I've told you many times over that ensuring your physical and mental well-being has always been one of my duties.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So, yes, even here, I still care about you. Even without a battle.

options: It's strange that you'd talk to me like this.
Alright.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Today's exam is over.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As I said, you don't need to report back here at the same time next week.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The regular morning and evening check-ups will continue for a while. Lancet-2 will look after you for me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If we ever find that your physical condition does not support your continued work, you must immediately return to Medical.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As for now, you may return to your work, Doctor.
4:32 P.M. \ Overcast, Visibility: 7 km
Rhodes Island Landship, Hallway outside the bridge

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: Earthspirit? What brings you here?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I've updated the geological monitoring report I submitted this morning.

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: You needed to make an adjustment so soon? That's unlike you.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: The numbers changed quickly. Made me miss my afternoon nap.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Forward the report to your team leader. My recommendations are at the bottom.

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: Sure. Strong winds warning, is it?

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: That's no problem. The Engineering Department strengthened the storm shutters two days in advance, and Logistics notified everyone to stay away from the at-risk deck areas.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: That's not all. Keep reading.

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: Huh... There might be a strong windstorm ahead of our route? Should we slow down or make a detour?

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: How dangerous is this windstorm you're talking about here?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I don't know.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: I looked at anomalies in the data and made my best call. All I know for sure is there's more than one cyclone forming ahead, and it's far more intense than anyone would expect.

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: Sounds pretty vague.

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: We set our route a month ago, it's already been approved. We're looking at a big mess if we change it on the fly.

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: You were in that meeting, right? We chose the route for its super low risk profile. Over the last decade, caravans from Lungmen to Leithanien have been back and forth over this route dozens of times.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Yes. In theory, we've avoided the Catastrophe-prone areas, and the probability of encountering danger is low.

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: But you're also not sure?

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: The bosses want us as far away from Ursus and Lungmen as soon as possible.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Whatever... I just needed to make sure you got my warning.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Deciding what to do with it is not in my job description. That's up to you.

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: Settle down, Earthspirit, we've got protocols. I'll notify the team leader, and we'll discuss...

options: There's no time for that.

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: Huh, Doctor?! Why are you here?

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: Shouldn't you be in your office?

options: I was going up onto the bridge.

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: Now that's some coincidence...

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: If you're taking the report, are you going to explain the situation to our team leader in person?

options: The windstorm is right in front of us. He'll notice soon enough.
The situation is urgent, I'll let Amiya know.

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: What? It's that serious? Well that's not good...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Doctor, you believe me?

options: I believe in reality.
I believe my operators.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Then I'll go to the bridge with you. I'll continue to observe the situation in real time and report to you and Amiya.

options: Good. That's the best option.
Not going to ask for overtime?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: This is within the scope of my duties.
4:39 P.M. \ Overcast, Visibility: 4 km
Rhodes Island Landship, Bridge

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: Warning, the wind speed is increasing rapidly!

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: At these numbers, our visibility's going to fall under one kilometer within a few minutes!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Did you turn on the assisted driving function for sandstorm mode?

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: We've had it on for a while, it was part of the itinerary.

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: But Amiya, this might not be an ordinary sandstorm...

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: My god!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What is it, Pavel?

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: Sensors detecting thunderstorm clouds ahead!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Open the PA, tell the whole ship that Rhodes Island will pass through a thunderstorm shortly, and raise the alert level by one!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Central command personnel, slow us down right now!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Ugh... we're rocking a lot...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What's the situation?

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: The pressure on the hull side panels is skyrocketing!

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: 70% of the outermost storm shutters have been damaged and are basically failing!

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: Also... multiple abnormal heat sources detected near the hull, energy amplitude approaching critical threshold!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Does this mean...

options: Yes. It's a Catastrophe.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Ah, Dr. {@nickname}!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: How... can this be?

options: No time to explain.
It's a supercell.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Alright... I got it.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: All hands, activate code red Catastrophe alert!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Evacuate all personnel on the first deck, bridge excluded. Gather all non-engineering personnel from the second to sixth levels in the central area for safety!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Central control, maintain minimum speed cruising...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Navigator, how long will this desert thunderstorm last?

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: These sudden-onset storms usually pass within an hour or two...

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: It's hard to say for sure. Doctor? Earthspirit?

options: Earthspirit, your analysis.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Yes, Doctor.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Mr. Pavel, the Doctor gave you the report I completed an hour ago.

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: Multiple small cyclones within two kilometers...? This doesn't bode well!

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: This Catastrophe is no ordinary desert thunderstorm... we could be looking at a maximum strength windstorm!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Can I borrow one of the sensors on the bridge?

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: Of course. I should've seen it myself...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It's alright, Mr. Pavel. This is an extremely abnormal phenomenon and well beyond the scope of normal Catastrophe prediction. An experienced Catastrophe Messenger would have some trouble spotting all the signs in time.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: If not for the Doctor's assistance, I would've treated the outliers as errors and glossed over them.

options: We still have time to move things in the right direction.
I'm getting a real bad feeling about this.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Doctor, Amiya, the small cyclones ahead are converging and intensifying.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: In other words, the core of the multi-cyclone vortex is about to generate.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Once the core forms, I estimate the cyclone will reach two kilometers in diameter and last at least seven to eight hours.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What happens if Rhodes Island maintains its speed as it approaches the core?

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: If we come into contact with the vortex, the ship's hull may collide with high-speed active Originium dust, roughly equivalent to the simultaneous detonation of hundreds of maximum-payload Originium bombs across the bulwark.

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: I'm sure you can guess how that might go for us.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Do we have enough time to change course?

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: I can try...

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: The core of the windstorm changes directions very quickly, and can reach a maximum speed of nearly 1,000 kilometers per hour.

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: Then there's no point in us trying.

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: Amiya, even if we try a full speed retreat, if we get unlucky with the direction, Rhodes Island won't escape the storm.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Then it seems like the only thing we can do is stay put.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Mr. Pavel, give me a potential damage assessment.

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: If we spend seven hours in a thunderstorm of a similar scale, the first to sixth decks will be damaged maybe 15%...

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: Of those, the first deck will take the hardest hits, and casualties are likely.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It'll be the biggest loss the ship takes in a year.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But, I don't see any options...

options: There is a way.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor?

options: We won't have to take damage.
You don't want to have to dock for a month of repairs, right?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes, if we have to stop in the wastelands, we could face other threats.

options: We have another choice.
Since we can't retreat and don't want to stop, what else can we do?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, are you suggesting that we continue straight ahead?

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: That's out of the question, visibility is too low!

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: Even with assisted driving, I can't navigate. I'm from Sargon, plunging headfirst into a sandstorm like this is suicide!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I understand your concerns, Mr. Kamal.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But, I trust the Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, are you sure about leading Rhodes Island through the Catastrophe zone?

options: I need Earthspirit to keep calculating the real-time coordinates of the vortex.
Yes.
I need PRTS to help me calculate the energy amplitude of the Originium on the surface.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Good, please cooperate with the Doctor.

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: Calculating a safe route in such a short time sounds like a bad joke.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If anyone can do it, it's our Doctor.

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: I've heard stories of the battles and all... but operating the landship is nothing like field command!

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: I don't know about this... Of course, I don't doubt the Doctor's abilities, but I've never heard of this real-time calculation method...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: It just might work...

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: Earthspirit, can you make sense of the Doctor's formulas?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: But they feel a bit familiar.

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Right... I heard about a similar formula from some whiz kid a couple days ago, but the Doctor's version is more complicated and varied.

options: I've given the route to the navigator.
Work with the central control staff if you need to change course rapidly.
Amiya, we're ready.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Let's head forward then!

options: I'll help you issue instructions.
Leave it to me.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No, Doctor, that would be too inefficient.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Rhodes Island only needs one commander right now.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Okay, Doctor, go forward until you're at my position.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: From the moment I saw you appear on the bridge, I trusted that the situation would definitely turn around.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Attention, everyone on the bridge–

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: From now on, I am transferring command of the Rhodes Island landship to Dr. {@nickname}!

options: Notify Closure and have her put all cabins into energy-saving mode!
All power to the engines!

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: Got it, Doctor!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Message from Closure: The engine is ready, and she wishes us 'good luck'...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: There's nothing wrong with going a little crazy every now and then.

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: If I knew I'd be sailing like this, I would've brought some booze.

options: Rhodes Island, all ahead full!

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: I'm getting a nosebleed from this speed!

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: That's because I elbowed your nose... Sorry, but the whole place is shaking so much I can't control my limbs.

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: Is the seismic damper malfunctioning?

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: Looks like it's not just my imagination - the whole ship's falling apart.

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: Earthspirit, you haven't taken your eyes off the screen at all...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Cyclone number two is continuing to move thirty degrees southeast, cyclone number three... cyclone number four...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, hold my hand!

options: I've got you, Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, did I step on your foot...?

options: Don't worry about it. You can hold on even tighter.
Your ears are making my face itchy.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Are we shaking less?

options: Hard right, now!!

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: Haah... I didn't even notice that strong wind just now. If it caught us, there's no telling if we would've been able to stabilize the hull at this speed!

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: Did the downburst make contact with the ground?

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Only two minutes until the core of the storm forms.

options: Maintain current trajectory and keep moving forward!

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: Wait, I see the cyclone!

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: There's one on the left and another on the right!

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: We're surrounded. Rhodes Island is going to collide in just two or three more minutes!

options: Keep going.

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: It's impossible to avoid them! We don't have enough space to maneuver!

options: Trust me.

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: I'm trying real hard, Doctor!

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: But I don't trust myself so much!

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: Forget it, if Amiya's with you, I'm on board too. Even if I have to tie my hand to the steering handle, I'll keep pushing it forward until the very end!

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: I just regret agreeing to swap shifts with that stinky lad, George...

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Seventy-five meters. Fifty meters. Thirty meters...

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: (Gulps nervously) I've never seen a Catastrophe-cyclone up close before...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor...

options: Amiya, are you afraid?
You're hurting my hand.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm a bit nervous, but I'm not afraid.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I am a little nervous. But rest assured, Doctor, I'm not afraid.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Sorry, Doctor, I'm a bit nervous. But I'm not afraid.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We've been through times like this together before.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The closer we might be to despair, the bigger everyone's hopes are, the more incredible the outcome will be.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, this is what you taught me.

options: Hope comes from the commitment to never give in, even at the bitter end.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes, Doctor, you once said the exact same words.
'Red alert, red alert...'
'Attention everyone, prepare for impact!'

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Just like before, we'll get through this crisis together.

options: Yes, we survived back then.
Look.
I think my record's looking pretty good.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The wind is subsiding... and the color of the sky is changing too.

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: Report, Rhodes Island has left the Catastrophe zone!!

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: The damage to all deck levels is less than 5%, and nobody was injured!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Thank goodness...

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: My nose hurtsssss... Pavel, do you know you hit my nose again?

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: So what if I did? We're alive, I say! Alive!

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: Fine, but you owe me a drink.

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: Whatever you want, it's on my tab. I almost made a big mistake.

steps.name: Navigator B
steps.text: Doctor, it's all thanks to you!

steps.name: Earthspirit
steps.text: Absolutely brilliant calculations, Doctor.

steps.name: Central Control Staff
steps.text: Doctor, is your command always so thrilling? Haha, I'd like to get another taste of that sometime!

steps.name: Navigator A
steps.text: Doctor, how in the world did you pull that off? It's like you've got prophetic Arts or something, suddenly showing up on the bridge right before we get hit by a Catastrophe!

options: To be fair, I was pretty anxious through that whole thing.
Shouldn't we celebrate?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor...

a.text: Amiya hugs you suddenly, and you realize that the hands on your waist are squeezing you tighter than they were at any point during the storm.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Thank you... Thank you standing by my side.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Not half bad.

options: I did what I had to do.
Thanks.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The relationship between the self-replication speed of Originium and the increase in energy— you applied this knowledge to the calculation of wind-Catastrophe trajectories.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You demonstrated similar abilities in the past, helping your colleagues at the time mitigate losses from Catastrophes. Some called you a Catastrophe expert.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But we both know what you really specialize in.

options: What do I specialize in?
Look, I really don't know.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That formula... You still remember it.

options: I didn't remember it before.
It jumped right into my head.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You created that formula yourself.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You've recovered a lot of information about Originium and Catastrophes over the past month, and you left a lot of calculations in your notes.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Perhaps the sudden crisis dredged up the latent memories from deep inside your consciousness, or perhaps you reinvented it using the knowledge you left behind.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The fact that you could recall this formula proves that you still retain a basic understanding of the nature of Originium.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In other words, you've never forgotten your identity as a researcher of Originium.

options: I want to continue this line of research.
This seems to be my duty.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You may see the study of Originium as your duty, but know that our actions should never be restricted by duty alone.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, what drives you to pursue the study of Originium so fervently?

options: Both you and Amiya have Oripathy.
The suffering caused by Originium scars our world.
I want to bring an end to this calamity.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I once heard an answer to this question.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It was very similar to what you said today, but also completely different.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The person who uttered those words had an instinctive desire to unravel truths unknown, and also worked hard to save lives.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But sometimes, salvation also meant destruction— that is what the same person told me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Do you still harbor that same answer deep within your brain?

options: Does it still count as being there even if I don't remember it?
Whatever makes you happy.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Amiya said your performance on the bridge today was much like that of an actual 'prophet.'

options: I did my homework.
Why are you staring at me like that?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The rational part of me wants to believe in science.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: When the results of your first brain examination came back, I thought I saw some errors in the process, and so there was a second time, a third time... and even a seventh time.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The rational part of me told me that repeating the same results three times was enough to prove that you weren't lying.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Without a shadow of a doubt, you really did lose a lot of your memories. You don't remember what you did to Theresa, and you forgot why you were standing here in the first place.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: All of this has caused a significant... dichotomy between you and the person I once knew.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But just like I allowed you to do the seventh test, in this moment, I once again find myself doubting... Who exactly is standing in front of me?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: How much of the past remains, and how much of you blooms anew?

options: You're being sentimental again.
It felt terrible having to sit through seven exams.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Perhaps, I won't deny it. Dealing with you always has a tendency to sway my emotions.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But this is also born of extreme rationality.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I hope you understand, there can be errors in our measurements. And in your case, I can no longer tolerate any errors.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I would like to apologize to you regarding this matter.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But taking a better grasp of your memory recuperation will also have real benefits for your body.

options: There's something I've wanted to ask for a long time.
Setting aside your role as a doctor, do you want me to regain my memories?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Situations are rarely black and white... and the same is true of human emotions.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I've not concealed my hatred for you in the past, but... no matter how much I hate to admit it, there's something else there too.

options: You want me doing everything I could before.
Do you miss the person you hate?
You're searching for the truth of the past.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If it's only strength I needed, I believe that you are good enough as you are... Perhaps, you can do even better.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Do I... 'miss'...?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That word is far too simple. The languages of this world have developed over thousands of years, and yet I am still unable to choose the most suitable word to order my thoughts during the many moments I think about you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Without a doubt, I seek that answer.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ideally, I want to hear the truth from your mouth. But I will not give up looking for that truth in other ways.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Now, it's my turn to ask you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, do you want your memories back?

options: I do.
I don't.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your answer doesn't matter. I see your hesitation.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Once your memories come back, many of your questions will be answered. However, not every answer will satisfy you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You will know where all the emotions pouring into you come from, whether it is the hatred from me and W, the unconditional trust from Amiya, or... even further back.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Excess memories, intense emotions, will instantly flood your entire brain—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Trust me, what you will feel at that time will be far greater than exhaustion.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What you should fear even more is, when the past finally catches up to you, you must decide.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What if those memories are too strong and engulf all the hard work you've put in recently, and pull you back into the abyss that you failed to crawl out of over countless years?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Once the current you is defeated, everything you've worked so hard to build will collapse, and your will may no longer be your own.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So, let me ask you once more—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, are you ready?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If luck is on our side, you won't need to answer this question any time soon.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I want to thank you. Over the past month or so, you've shown me some new possibilities.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Especially today. I learned that you still remember the formula.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It turns out, you and I are not the only ones preparing for that day.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I suspected this long ago, that home-use life functions restoration device was not supposed to have the defect of deleting one's memory—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In particular, it's impossible to selectively delete the part of the brain most likely involved in decision-making, but still retaining the parts most meaningful to you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}......

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What I think is, she trusted you even more than I could fathom in the past.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That being the case, we should continue to work hard.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Just as I've said countless times already, I will help you, as long as we continue to stand together.
7:43 P.M. \ Overcast
Rhodes Island Landship, Command Center
Professor, are you here?

options: Eyjafjalla? Come in.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Professor, they said you wanted to see me...

options: This is for you.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Is it about my application to become an operator...? Oh, it's been approved?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: That's great news. Everyone said you and Miss Amiya would turn me down because of my condition.

options: I convinced her.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: I see, you even went out of your way to get it approved? Thank you...

options: The briefing you submitted this morning helped Rhodes Island through a crisis.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: You mean... the Catastrophe this afternoon?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Professor, did you read my analysis?

options: Your Originium vein expansion observations were incredibly accurate.
You were able to predict a Catastrophe through an increase in Originium activation on the surface.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: It was just a hunch.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: They said the density of Originium near the surface around here would be very low, but I saw the same situation in a volcano in southern Leithanien...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Even a small amount of Originium proliferates rapidly over a brief period when the conditions are right.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Two days ago, after finishing my daily treatment, I was walking around the dorms as usual when I saw the approaching phenomenon from the dust samples on the porthole.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: In sandy terrain, a sudden burst in Originium energy will cause the ground temperature to rise rapidly, leading to a significant increase in the possibility of large-scale wind-Catastrophes.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Um... I'm so sorry... I can go on and on about this stuff...

options: Please continue.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: You've already seen the report, right?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Busy as you are, I never expected you'd read our random notes.

options: I also read your thesis.
Your research is very interesting.
I've said before, I'm a hard worker, but some folks are thinking I can use Arts.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Professor, are you interested in my research?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Do mystical Originium Arts like that exist?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Ah... I understand, you were making a joke.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: If you're not too busy, I'd love to stay over and have a nice chat with you again.

options: After I get some work done.
You're welcome to look around.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: There are so many books on your desk...

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Annals of the Great Yan Classics,' 'A Tower Without a Legend,' 'Columbia Judicial Observation Notes,' 'Conquest and Assimilation' ...Professor, are these the books you normally read?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Your interests are so diverse. It's nothing like the bookcases of the other professors I know.

options: I think this one will interest you the most.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: These are your... Catastrophe research notes?

options: Just something to read over.
Just some thoughts I jotted down.
Just a rough draft.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Thank you... Thank you so much! I'll study these thoroughly!

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: If I have any questions, may I come to talk to you?

options: Any time.
You're always welcome.
As long as I can finish my other work.

a.text: The young scholar clutches the notes you handed her tightly, lifts her head, and looks at you with conviction-filled eyes.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Professor... my life has been a series of wonderful surprises since coming to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: The stability of my Oripathy has given me a lot more confidence about my future, and people like you have given me the hope to keep moving forward.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: If you're working so hard, then what reason do any of us have to give up?

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: —Professor.

steps.name: Eyjafjalla
steps.text: Thank you so much for leading Rhodes Island forward, and on into the future.
